item.title: Conservative Media Personality Makes Runoff for Alaska Governor
item.description: Bernadette Wilson, who has appealed to other Republicans to consolidate around her party’s top finisher, will be one of four finalists on the ranked-choice ballot in November.
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin

item.media:description: Bernadette Wilson, a conservative Republican, is one of the 17 candidates running for governor in Alaska’s primary.

item.title: In Headache for Republicans, Second Dan Sullivan Advances in Alaska Senate Race

item.media:description: Dan J. Sullivan in Petersburg, Alaska, this summer.

item.title: Graham, and Trump, Triumph: Six Takeaways From South Carolina’s Senate Runoff
item.description: President Trump went all in for Senator Darline Graham in a primary runoff on Tuesday. It worked, preserving his undefeated streak in Republican Senate primaries this year.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei
item.media:credit: Sean Rayford for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham’s victory on Tuesday showed President Trump’s continued ability to move Republican primary voters, especially when he goes all in on a race.

item.title: Darline Graham, Backed By Trump, Wins Primary for Senate in South Carolina
item.description: Ms. Graham, who is temporarily filling the seat long held by her late brother, Senator Lindsey Graham, prevailed in a runoff and will be heavily favored in November.

item.media:description: Senator Darline Graham has won her party’s nomination to compete for a full, six-year term in November.

item.title: Everton Blair Jr. Wins Race to Fill David Scott’s House Seat in Georgia

item.title: Democrats Score Victory in Campaign Finance Court Case
item.description: Republicans had hoped that a Supreme Court decision allowing party committees to coordinate with candidates would also entitle them to lower ad rates. On Tuesday, an appeals court said otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: Kendrick Brinson for The New York Times
item.media:description: Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia was one of four Democratic candidates who prevailed in a lawsuit restricting ad prices for party committees. Republicans, whose committees are flush with cash, were seeking lower rates available only to candidates.
